It appears to be related to memory usage: whenever I start the Gradle process (e.g., test or build), the local server hangs. Usually, the memory consumption is at this time very high: around 80% on a 64 GB Windows machine. Gradle seems to use memory/threads very aggressively, so this problem can be reproduced every time Gradle runs. It makes OpenCode in practice **very** uncomfortable to use - I have to restart it after every Gradle run and continue a stopped task, or direct AI not to use Gradle to test changes. That's the major reason I prefer an OpenAI local agent, although all other features of OpenCode are good enough for me and subscriptions are competitive.

I would say that if you want to reproduce, just use OpenCode to make the changes in a Gradle project and start tests.

The docs already specify the bound this issue asks for —
https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/compaction states that during summary generation "tools disabled and **at
most 4096 output tokens**" are used. The tools half is implemented (`tools: []`); the output half is
not implemented anywhere.

At `39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe`, the compaction request passes no `generation` field:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L274-L282

`LLM.request` accepts `generation` (`packages/ai/src/llm.ts:41-51`), and OpenAI-compatible lowering
reads it at `packages/ai/src/protocols/open-responses.ts:573`
(`max_output_tokens: generation?.maxTokens`), so an unset field leaves `max_output_tokens` absent and
the provider falls back to the model's own limit — 131,072 in this report.

`4096` appears exactly once in `packages/ai`, as an Anthropic-protocol fallback used only when the
model catalog carries no output limit (`anthropic-messages.ts:620`). It never applies to the
OpenAI-compatible route, so on those providers compaction is unbounded on every model.

So this is a doc/code mismatch as much as a bug: the documented contract is 4096, and passing
`generation: { maxTokens: 4096 }` on the compaction request would implement it. Worth aligning with
`SessionCompaction.required()`, which already reserves `Math.min(limits.output, 32_000)` when
computing the threshold — the reservation and the actual request currently disagree.

Question rather than a bug report — is the numeric-string case intentional?

`finite()` takes a `number`, so a cost field that arrives as a numeric string now prices at 0, where `?? 0` used to hand it straight to decimal.js, which parses it fine:

| `cost.input` | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"3"` | 3 | 0 |
| `"1e3"` | 1000 | 0 |
| `{}` | threw | 0 ✅ |

If the answer is "a string violates the declared `Schema.Finite`, so we don't support it", that's a perfectly good answer and I'll drop it — the crash was the real problem and that's fixed. I'm asking because the failure mode flipped from loud to silent (an under-reported cost rather than an aborted turn), and because the same shape just landed in `packages/core` via #43251, so whichever way you want it, it probably wants to be the same in both.

Happy to send a patch if you'd like the string path kept.

I hope that this fix/feature will be implemented somehow. Analogously to other agentic tools, read permissions could influence grep permissions implicitly, e.g. by filtering matches afterwards.

However, permissions based on grep patterns is rather useless IMHO.

**Additional real-world data point (opencode 1.18.18, local model via OpenAI-compatible / llama.cpp)**

Confirmed still present on **1.18.18** (issue was reported against 1.17.14). Our stack: custom OpenAI-compatible provider (local llama.cpp server) running a 27B Q8_0 model with declared limit `{ context: 262144, output: 32768 }` (no `input`), and `compaction: { auto: true, prune: true, tail_turns: 2, reserved: 80000 }`.

**Empirically measured threshold from the session DB:**
- total = 229,165 tokens → no compaction
- total = 230,697 tokens → auto-compaction fired
- implied threshold = 229,376 = 262144 − 32768 = `context − maxOutputTokens`, exactly branch B. `reserved: 80000` had zero effect.

**User-visible harm (why this matters beyond a silent no-op):**
This model's output quality degrades (verbatim context repetition loops + early EOS, i.e. truncated outputs) once context reaches ~71–73% of the window (~185–190k of 262k). The effective trigger (229k) sat ~40k **above** the degeneration onset, so the model degraded well before compaction ever fired — the session became unusable and had to be abandoned. The whole point of `reserved` is to pull the trigger earlier; branch B silently disables it at exactly the moment it is needed.

**Verified workaround (custom providers):**
Adding `"limit": { "input": 240000, "context": 262144, "output": 32768 }` to the custom provider's model entry activates branch A: usable = 240000 − 80000 = **160,000** → auto-compaction now fires at 160k, safely before the degeneration onset. So custom/local providers (OpenAI-compatible, local inference servers) *can* work around this in config — unlike the built-in-provider case called out in the issue, where no override path exists.

**Suggestion:**
When branch B is selected and `cfg.compaction.reserved` is explicitly set, either
1. apply `reserved` in branch B as well (`context − maxOutputTokens − reserved`), or
2. emit a visible warning that `compaction.reserved` is being ignored because the model has no `limit.input`.

A silent no-op on a user-facing knob is a UX trap: users believe a safety margin is in force when it isn't.

Happy to share the full incident analysis (timestamps, DB compaction parts, llama.cpp log excerpts) on request.

I think I have the mechanism for this, and the short version is that the write tokens aren't missing —
they're being recorded as `input`.

### Where it happens

`mapUsage` derives the non-cached portion by subtraction:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/open-responses.ts#L593-L609

Both fields are `Schema.optional` on `input_tokens_details`. When a route sends `cached_tokens` but no
`cache_write_tokens`, `cacheWrite` is `undefined`, so it contributes nothing to the subtraction and
the tokens that were written to cache stay inside `nonCached`. Downstream, `SessionUsage.tokens`
coerces the undefined write to `0` via `safe()`, and the same tokens are already sitting in `input`.

So `cache.write = 0` isn't a dropped field. It's a misclassification, and it's silent because the
arithmetic still balances.

### The natural experiment

My database has both kinds of route side by side, which makes this easy to check. Average `input` per
request, for every model with at least 250 requests that reported `cache.read > 0`:

| provider / model | requests | avg `input` | avg `cache.write` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic/claude-opus-5` | 4,634 | **2** | 16,018 |
| `openai/astra` | 4,984 | **3** | 6,301 |
| `opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna` | 276 | **3** | 81,910 |
| `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` | 13,179 | **4,860** | 0 |
| `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` | 11,955 | **6,231** | 0 |
| `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` | 51,202 | **21,065** | 0 |

Every route that reports a cache write has an average `input` of two to three tokens. Every route that
doesn't carries thousands. That's the same quantity showing up in a different column, not two
different behaviours.

The obvious alternative — that these models simply miss cache more often, so the extra `input` is
genuinely uncached content rather than an unlabelled write — is ruled out by the filter. Every row in
these tables had `cache.read > 0`, and you cannot read from a cache that nothing wrote. Caching is
demonstrably active on exactly the requests reporting zero writes. The only remaining reading is that
the writes happened and weren't labelled.

`gpt-5.6-luna` is the cleanest pair: on `opencode-go` it reports 81,910 average write and 3 average
input; on `openai` it reports 0 write and 21,065 average input. Same model, same account.

### How much

Because it's a reclassification rather than a loss, this can be measured directly instead of
extrapolated. Summing `input` over requests that also had `cache.read > 0`:

| provider / model | requests | `input` recorded | `cache.read` | share of prompt volume filed as `input` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` | 51,202 | 1,078,547,903 | 3.62B | 22.9% |
| `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` | 11,955 | 74,492,643 | 1.12B | 6.2% |
| `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` | 13,179 | 64,044,087 | 1.61B | 3.8% |
| `openai/astra` | 4,984 | 14,952 | 0.38B | 0.0% |
| `anthropic/claude-opus-5` | 4,634 | 9,268 | 0.93B | 0.0% |

That's **1.217 billion tokens** on the `openai` provider alone that would have been booked as
`cache.write` on a reporting route. The two reporting models round to 0.0%.

The billing consequence follows from that: those tokens are priced at the input rate rather than the
cache-write rate, so the cost is understated by the write premium on 1.2B tokens rather than being
wrong by 100%. That is probably why the discrepancy showed up as a surprise on the invoice rather than
as an obviously broken number.

### Same signature elsewhere

The pattern isn't OpenAI-specific — it's every route that omits the field:

| provider / model | requests | avg `input` | avg `cache.write` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xai/grok-4.6` | 5,015 | 10,414 | 0 |
| `xai/grok-4.3` | 859 | 8,919 | 0 |
| `opencode-go/minimax-m3` | 9,028 | 3,288 | 0 |
| `opencode-go/glm-5.2` | 253 | 13,015 | 0 |

`xai` is the most absolute case: 5,892 assistant messages, `max(cache.write)` and `sum(cache.write)`
both exactly zero, across two models. If a regression test is w

I went looking for this in V2 at `39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe`. It didn't survive the
port, because the step topology changed rather than the assignment being fixed.

### V2 issues one request per step

`llm.ts` doesn't loop steps inside a call. A call returns an outcome, and continuation re-enters with
an incremented step:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts#L165

The event publisher is constructed inside that per-call function, at
[`llm.ts:284`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts#L284),
and that is its only call site in the tree. So each step gets its own request, its own publisher, its
own settlement, and its own assistant message. There is no object that several steps' usage could be
folded into.

### And the settlement is guarded anyway

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts#L495-L499

Still an assignment, but a second `step-finish` on one publisher is a hard `Effect.die`. Even if the
topology above changed, this would crash rather than silently under-report.

### The helper this issue asks for already exists

[`usage.ts:44-55`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/usage.ts#L44-L55)
is the accumulating fold, and it's used in the two places where one logical call really does stream
several `step-finish` events — `SessionCompaction.execute` and `SessionTitle` both do
`usage = usage ? SessionUsage.add(usage, step) : step`.

Worth noting it sums every field including `input` and `cache.read`, which is the opposite of what
this issue proposes for those two. That's correct for compaction and title, where each step is a
separate prompt, and would be wrong for a multi-step agentic turn where the final request already
contains the earlier ones. So if the V2 topology ever does change, `SessionUsage.add` isn't the right
fold to reach for as-is.

### Corroboration from data

105,379 assistant messages against 4,309 user ones — a 24:1 ratio consistent with a new assistant
message per round-trip. Individual messages carry two to seven tool parts (14,349 with one, 1,473 with
two, 1,129 with three), which is parallel calls inside a single step, not sequential steps.
it would be nice

Still reproducible on v1.18.17 on a phone. Switching apps or letting the phone sleep leaves the current conversation frozen even though the response continues server-side.

Besides reloading, switching session tabs or toggling from the main agent to a subagent (or back) immediately reveals the missing updates. That suggests those navigation paths resync session state while returning the existing tab to the foreground does not. This is fixed for local CLI use and still open for the workerd server path. My instance has an empty
`event` table, and the reason is a specific commit rather than a general improvement.

### The numbers first

`0.0.0-beta-17498`, after heavy use — 114,870 session messages across 3,245 costed sessions:

```
page_size=4096  page_count=462232  → 1.89 GB
freelist_count=1085
```

| table | rows | size |
|---|---|---|
| `session_message` | 114,870 | 1.53 GB |
| `part` | 38,353 | 0.11 GB |
| `message` | 10,359 | 0.02 GB |
| `event` | 0 | 0 |
| `event_sequence` | 3,246 | ~0 |

### Why it's zero

Event persistence became opt-in, defaulting to off, in
[`120e4e7388af61c1b9274b58a16b6e3f9878699c`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/120e4e7388af61c1b9274b58a16b6e3f9878699c)
— "fix(core): make event persistence opt-in", 2026-08-05, about six weeks after this issue was filed.

The flag lands here:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/bus.ts#L199

The insert is gated on it (`bus.ts:590`) while `EventSequenceTable` is written unconditionally
(`bus.ts:586`). That asymmetry is the fingerprint to look for: on a fixed instance `event_sequence`
keeps accumulating rows while `event` stays empty, which is exactly what mine shows — 3,246 against 0.

### Who still persists

One production caller turns it on — the workerd server runtime:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/server/src/workerd.ts#L69

On that path nothing in the original report has changed. The only cleanup is `remove(aggregateID)` at
`bus.ts:673-681`, which drops one aggregate's rows inside a transaction and is not a retention policy —
no TTL, no row cap, no size limit. An aggregate that stays live accumulates indefinitely, so the 13 GB
growth described here is still reachable there.

This still reproduces by construction on `0.0.0-beta-17498`, and the fix surface is smaller than the
original report assumed.

The key is a pure function of the session id and nothing else:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/prompt-cache-key.ts#L5-L6

Every call site passes the live session id — `model-request.ts:223`, `generate-node.ts:72`,
`compaction.ts:277` — so a fork, being a new session id, necessarily gets a new key while sending the
parent's prefix.

The suggested fix is already supported by the schema without new storage: `session_v2` carries
`fork_session_id` and `fork_boundary` columns, and `make()` consults neither. Resolving the fork chain
to its root inside `make()` would fix all three call sites at once, since they all go through it.

One thing worth deciding at the same time. That single key is shared by the main conversation,
compaction and title generation, and compaction in particular sends a deliberately divergent prefix
under it — `tools: []`, one user message, a different serialization
([`compaction.ts:274-282`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L274-L282)).
So the question isn't only "which id should a fork key on" but "what is this key scoped to at all". A
fix that resolves fork roots and separates the auxiliary calls into their own keyspace would settle
both; fixing forks alone leaves the second half in place.

The lifetime-counter observation still holds on `0.0.0-beta-17498` — the session totals are cumulative
adds, exactly as quoted, at
[`projector.ts:59-63`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/projector.ts#L59-L63).

The part worth checking is the conditional: "dangerous if any compaction / routing / provider request /
context-window logic treats cumulative session usage as if it represented the current prompt size." I
grepped every reader of those columns to find out whether anything does.

### Where they get read, and what for

Four places read `tokens_input`, `tokens_cache_read` and their siblings. Every one of them is a
display or transport path:

- `info.ts:38-46` decodes them into `Session.Info.tokens` — the shape the API and TUI render.
- `projector.ts:71-95` selects them and publishes `SessionEvent.UsageUpdated`. That event is declared
  `Event.ephemeral`, so it isn't even persisted, and nothing in core subscribes to it; it exists to
  push a number at connected clients.
- `transfer.ts:113-117` carries the totals along when a session moves between instances.
- `v1-migration.bun.ts` backfills them once from per-message tokens.

Nothing in compaction, routing, provider request assembly or context-window accounting consults them.

Compaction in particular reads the last assistant message, never the session row:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts#L367-L386

So the 41M cumulative `cache.read` in the original report can't reach the compaction trigger. My
database bears that out from the other direction: sessions carry lifetime `cache.read` in the billions
— 6.74B on `openai` alone — while their per-message `cache.read` tracks the real prompt size and
compaction fires normally throughout.

### Which leaves two separate things

The counters are a presentation problem. The number in `opencode stats` is a lifetime sum that reads
like a context measurement, and relabelling or documenting it would remove the alarm without changing
any behaviour.

The context-window failure is a different bug that this report may have misattributed. If it still
reproduces on V2 it deserves its own issue, and the useful diagnostic is the *last assistant message's*
tokens at the point of failure rather than the session total — that's the number the trigger actually
sees. Worth checking #42448 too, which has compaction itself blowing the context window through an
unbounded output budget; that failure looks a lot like this one from the outside.

V1's analysis pointed at `packages/opencode/src/session/llm/ai-sdk.ts`. V2 rewrote the provider layer
into `packages/ai/src/protocols/`, and the same gap is now here:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts#L582-L600

This is the path every OpenAI-compatible provider takes. `openai-compatible-chat.ts` doesn't define
its own protocol — it reuses `OpenAIChat.protocol` end to end and overrides only the route id:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-compatible-chat.ts#L17-L23

So litellm, vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama-compat and every gateway fronting Anthropic all land on that one
`mapUsage`, which reads cache counts only from `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and
`prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens`. A gateway reporting `cache_creation_input_tokens` at the
top level of `usage` — exactly the payload in your report — matches neither key.

### Why this fails silently, which I think is the more important half

The two protocols use opposite conventions, and only one of them can hide a missing field.

Native Anthropic **adds up**:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts#L686-L700

`input_tokens` there is exclusive of cache, so `inputTokens = nonCached + cacheRead + cacheWrite`. Drop
a field on that path and the *total* comes out too small — visible, and something downstream can catch.

OpenAI Chat **subtracts**: `prompt_tokens` is inclusive, so `nonCached = prompt_tokens - (cached +
cacheWrite)`. Drop `cacheWrite` here and the total stays perfectly correct — the tokens simply move
into the `nonCached` column. Nothing reconciles wrong, no invariant breaks, no total looks off. The
bill is the only place the difference is observable, which is why this keeps getting refiled per
provider (#35974, #37745, this one) instead of being caught once.

That also means your cost estimate is understated by more than the 1.25x you mentioned whenever the
provider prices cache writes above input, and it is *silently* understated in every case.

### The fix needs no schema change

The alternate keys already survive decoding. Both the `usage` struct and `prompt_tokens_details` are
declared with a rest record:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts#L155-L181

`Schema.StructWithRest(..., [Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Unknown)])` keeps unknown keys on the
decoded value, so `cache_creation_input_tokens` is present on the object `mapUsage` already receives.
Reading it there is additive — no schema edit, no new plumbing.

One caveat worth stating, because it constrains *where* the fix can go: `mapUsage` sets
`providerMetadata: { openai: usage }`, but that does not survive persistence. I checked 105,379
assistant rows in my database and none carries a `providerMetadata` key — the persisted message keeps
only `agent, model, content, finish, cost, tokens, time, snapshot, error`. So a downstream fallback
that reads provider metadata off the stored message cannot work; it has to happen inside `mapUsage`
while the raw payload is still in hand.

### Scope

#35974 is the same function and the same gap, with DeepSeek's key names instead. Both are one patch.

This is the same gap as #36749, in the same function, and the two are one patch rather than two.

On V2 (`0.0.0-beta-17498`) the DeepSeek route goes through the shared OpenAI Chat protocol —
`openai-compatible-chat.ts` reuses `OpenAIChat.protocol` end to end — and the mapping reads cache
counts only from `prompt_tokens_details`:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts#L582-L600

DeepSeek reports `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` / `prompt_cache_miss_tokens` at the top level of `usage`
(per your report — I have no DeepSeek traffic to verify the wire shape myself), so neither key is
matched. #36749 hits the identical wall with a gateway sending `cache_creation_input_tokens`.

Both keys already survive decoding, because the usage struct carries a rest record:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts#L155-L181

So the fix is additive inside `mapUsage` — read the provider's own key names before falling back to
the subtraction. No schema change.

Worth flagging why nobody notices until the bill arrives: `prompt_tokens` is inclusive, and `nonCached`
is derived as `prompt_tokens - (cached + cacheWrite)`. With `cacheWrite` undefined the miss tokens stay
inside `nonCached` and the totals still reconcile exactly, so `cache.write: 0` is not accompanied by
any other symptom. Your requested `hit / (hit + miss)` ratio is unrecoverable from the stored message
for the same reason — `providerMetadata` is not persisted, so the raw counts are gone by then.

Reproduced and quantified on a 1.89 GB production database (V2, `0.0.0-beta-17498`): 3,246 sessions,
114,870 `session_message` rows. I ran this on a copy, so the deletions below are real, not modelled.

### Baseline — the freelist looks harmless right up until you delete something

```
page_size       4096
page_count      462,233     → 1,893,306,368 bytes
freelist_count  1,085       → 4.4 MB, 0.23% of the file
auto_vacuum     0 (NONE)
```

Almost all of it is live data, not slack — `session_message` alone is 1.678 GB of the 1.893 GB
(105,379 assistant rows averaging 13.7 KB each). On a never-deleted instance this issue is invisible,
which I suspect is why it has stayed open: nothing looks wrong until the first bulk delete.

### Deleting half the sessions strands 855 MB that never comes back

`session_message` cascades from `session_v2` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), so deleting sessions removes their
messages. Deleting 1,623 of 3,246 sessions dropped 51,849 message rows:

```
                 page_count    freelist_count    file size
before            462,233           1,085        1,893,306,368
after delete      462,233         208,655        1,893,306,368
```

Not one byte returned to the filesystem, and 855 MB — 45% of the file — became free pages. That is
exactly the behaviour described in the report.

`VACUUM` does recover it: 1,893,306,368 → 1,005,211,648 bytes, **888 MB reclaimed, 46.9%**, in 11.3 s
wall on this database.

### The migration detail that will bite whoever implements this

`PRAGMA auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL` is a no-op on an existing database. Measured on the same snapshot:

```
PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL;  PRAGMA auto_vacuum;   →  0    (unchanged)
PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL;  VACUUM;  PRAGMA auto_vacuum;   →  2    (INCREMENTAL)
```

The mode only changes when a full `VACUUM` rewrites the file, so setting the pragma at connection open
fixes new databases and silently does nothing for every existing one. Shipping this needs a one-time
migration `VACUUM` — 11.3 s here, and it needs a progress signal or it will look like a hang on
startup (compare #38561, #35514, #41739).

Once the mode is actually INCREMENTAL, reclamation no longer needs a full rebuild:

```
after delete (INCREMENTAL)     freelist 200,272    file 1,828,679,680
after PRAGMA incremental_vacuum freelist       0    file 1,007,357,952
```

821 MB returned without a rewrite. That is the `vacuum()` utility the issue asks for, and it is cheap
enough to run on a schedule.

### One correction to the thread

@skywalker-35's 36 GB case is attributed to `part.data` accumulating tool output. That was V1's
layout. On this V2 instance `part` is a migration leftover: its newest row is dated 2026-07-03 while
`session_message` is current to today, and no V2 code path writes it. It sits at 128 MB against
`session_message`'s 1.678 GB. Same failure, different table — a retention policy aimed at `part` would
now miss almost all of the bytes.

Note that auto_vacuum addresses only reclamation after deletion. It does nothing about growth itself —
1.89 GB from 3,246 sessions with nothing deleted is a separate question about assistant-message
payload retention.

On V2 (`0.0.0-beta-17498`) this mapping exists. `openai-chat.ts` reads
`prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` into `cacheReadInputTokens`, and every OpenAI-compatible
provider reuses that protocol unmodified:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts#L582-L600

Streaming is wired up as well — `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` is set on every request
(`openai-chat.ts:548`), so the final chunk carrying `cached_tokens` is both requested and parsed.

### What can still lose the value on this path

Usage state is replaced rather than merged. `openai-chat.ts:692`:

```ts
const usage = mapUsage(event.usage) ?? state.usage
```

The last chunk carrying any usage object wins outright. A proxy that emits usage more than once in a
stream — a chunk with `prompt_tokens_details`, then a bare `prompt_tokens` totals chunk — loses the
cache read to the second one. The native Anthropic protocol has no such exposure; it folds per-field
rather than replacing:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/39be1595993de57a5a667c86e21ff788a80ebbbe/packages/ai/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts#L709-L716

This fits the contrast in the report, where zhipu and minimax record cache correctly and only the
litellm route reports zero — it would be a property of how that proxy chunks usage rather than of the
mapping. Unconfirmed: no litellm traffic available here to reproduce against.

The raw SSE tail from a single litellm request settles it. If `usage` appears in more than one `data:`
frame, that is the cause.

### Narrowing which layer drops it

`tokens_cache_read` on the session row is a cumulative projection, one step removed from what the
protocol produced. The per-message value splits the problem (V2 schema below; on 1.17.x the equivalent
is the `message` table filtered on `$.role`):

```
opencode db "SELECT json_extract(data,'$.tokens.cache.read')
             FROM session_message WHERE type='assistant'
             ORDER BY time_created DESC LIMIT 10"
```

Non-zero per-message against a zero session total puts the loss in the rollup. Zero in both means it
never survived `mapUsage`.

> **Solucionado al separar los permisos del agente padre de los permisos de la sesión padre.**
>
> `TaskTool` obtiene los permisos de la sesión hija a partir de `parent.permission`, que representa los permisos de la sesión padre, en lugar de heredar directamente los permisos configurados en el agente padre. Posteriormente, el subagente se evalúa utilizando sus propios `agent.permission` junto con los permisos derivados de su sesión.
>
> Como resultado, un `deny` configurado en el agente padre ya no se propaga a la sesión hija y, por tanto, ya no puede sobrescribir un permiso explícitamente permitido en el subagente delegado.

| cache read | $0.007 / 1M | 531k × $0.007 / 1M ≈ **$0.0037** → the $0.004 rows |
| uncached input | $0.22 / 1M | 532,116 × $0.22 / 1M = **$0.11707** → the $0.117 rows |

Usage History is reporting a real miss: that whole prefix was billed as uncached input. The prompt only grew a few hundred tokens per turn — a normal append — so a prefix-stable cache should have kept hitting.

Two misses in a row (10:03 and 10:04) also rules out a one-shot eviction. DeepSeek writes the prefix at the end of a request; the next request on the same backend should hit.

https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/kv_cache

Staying at cache read 0 means either the next request left that cache domain, or the hit was not the field Go reads.

### 1. The gateway can leave the cache domain without the client changing anything

Session is only pinned when the model has `stickyProvider` set. Otherwise the tracker is a no-op:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/9e22c40ffffe82566c00e4a4ad31e7ac3d973d44/packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/stickyProviderTracker.ts#L4-L10

Provider selection then hashes the last four characters of the session id over the *current* provider pool. The pool is filtered live by TPM, TPS, and budget — and a 530k miss itself pushes TPM, which can shrink the pool on the very next turn:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/9e22c40ffffe82566c00e4a4ad31e7ac3d973d44/packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/handler.ts#L643-L653

#35402 already showed this on GLM-5.2 with byte-identical requests: warm, then a full miss, then warm again, with the usage JSON shape flipping between two upstreams. Flash was the stable control in #31348. This report is the same cliff on Flash.

### 2. Or the hit is in a field Go does not read

Go’s OpenAI-compatible mapper only accepts `cached_tokens` / `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. It never reads DeepSeek’s `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`. An upstream that only emits the native field would look like cache read 0 and bill as input even if the prefix hit:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/9e22c40ffffe82566c00e4a4ad31e7ac3d973d44/packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/provider/openai-compatible.ts#L61-L70

That is a different bug from a hop, and it is easy to tell apart from the same two usage rows.

### How to tell them apart

Look at `provider` (or `x-opencode-endpoint-id`) on the 10:02 vs 10:03 rows:

- **It changes** → real hop. Enable `stickyProvider: "prefer"` for `deepseek-v4-flash`, the same fix #35402 asked for on GLM.
- **It stays put**, and the raw upstream usage has `prompt_cache_hit_tokens > 0` → read that field in `normalizeUsage`.
- **It stays put** and the upstream also reports 0 → a real prefix miss on one backend (tools/system first-byte change, or DeepSeek best-effort). That needs a prefix hash, as in #31348.

The $0.117 is the correct uncached list price. The product bug is either losing the warm cache domain or dropping the hit field. Quota from those miss rows is a support restore once one of the first two checks lands.
